analysis.title: Network Thoughts: Cautious But Confident in Europe; Inflation Worries In Australia
key_insights: UBS European Conference (record 1,700 investors, 160+ companies): broad regional growth is lacking. Growth is concentrated in structural-capex sectors with visible demand and scarce capacity: grid, electrification, datacenter infrastructure, defence, energy infrastructure, industrial automation and mining. Companies in these areas report tight supply out to 2028/29, with their own capacity the potential limit.
European Industrials and Tech are supplying the AI build-out. Data companies, logistics and insurers are monetising AI or gaining efficiencies from it.

Inflation is evident across European sectors and most companies expect to pass some or all of it through. Pricing power could be scarce for companies under competitive pressure (European autos) or that are labour-heavy (retail, delivery).

With limited growth, European companies are cutting fixed costs, rationalising production capacity and divesting non-core assets. With no broad consumer green shoots, the sector is the busiest for M&A. Little mention of high rates causing balance sheet stress, and disposal proceeds are likely returned to shareholders.
European banks have moved from balance-sheet repair to profitability, distributions and selective growth. The three listed exchanges in attendance all talked positively of growth.

European Conference investor polling: two-thirds expect government debt to end in some form of monetisation, 63% believe western governments have made false economic promises, and about 88% say French sovereign spreads have yet to peak. A majority remain bullish on US equities and 62% back equities as 2027's best-performing asset class.
Most investors at the conference expect AI's disinflationary impact only after 2028. Rising leverage and private-credit stress topped the list of underestimated private-market risks.

UBS Australasia Conference (1,900 investors, 147 companies, Sydney): RBA and RBNZ speakers were hawkish on inflation. Australia has had five rate hikes this year, dwelling prices are down 7% since March, home loans fell 15% last quarter, and rates are at 15-year highs.

UBS's Australia equity strategist reports earnings forecasts falling at the fastest pace since Covid. The year-end ASX index target is a few percent below current spot. Commodities and capex-related businesses are holding up relatively well while the consumer is weak.

In Australia, the AI build-out appears to be feeding the RBA's inflation concerns, with little evidence yet of a productivity gain. UBS's AI speakers were more optimistic on productivity gains later in the decade.

Sovereign debt: the best hope is that governments muddle through, since fiscal repair needs growth that is hard to generate and spending cuts that are politically unpalatable. The bearish outcome is sovereign yields grinding higher with gold as the hedge. The optimistic case is that markets tolerate deteriorating fundamentals while politicians signal restraint. France looks like the exception, where the political path to reassuring bond markets is exceptionally narrow.

Hedge funds: gross exposure remains elevated in the US and Europe after six weeks of AI-unwind volatility. Sharp de-grossing days have been followed by quick re-grossing. The volatility of gross flows is higher than at any point in UBS Knowledge Network data. Nets are tighter through increased hedging.
Short exposure has risen rapidly to highs across the US and Europe. UBS sees a greater chance that good or no news triggers an 'unloved rally' into year end, and expects muted hedge fund activity.

Fed: Chair Warsh's reluctance to give forward guidance leaves him looking like a consensus follower. Governor Waller suggested strong inflation could warrant a 50bp hike in December. UBS views 50bp in December versus 25bp in both December and January as largely optics. Williams and Jefferson are seen as the pivotal voices, and Jefferson speaks Friday at 19:00 New York.

Market pricing after the week's commentary: 28bp of tightening for Dec 9 and a further 17bp for Jan 27. This adds a full 25bp to the hiking cycle and takes the terminal rate to almost 4.75% by next September.

US CPI was hot and broad-based against expectations of a low-20bp core print. Core goods rose 16bp, core services 34bp and supercore 40bp. Shelter's 3-month annualised pace reached 3.1%, transportation services rose 1.5% m/m and food rose 41bp.

US 2-year yields rose about 18bp Monday and about 14bp Wednesday, about 34bp for the week to date. The 95th-percentile daily rise in 2s is about 13bp versus 5.8bp in the 2010s. The rate repricing pushed BBDXY to one-year highs, while hedge-fund USD positioning remains relatively light.

Data centre scrutiny: since the US midterms, policy is moving toward making hyperscalers responsible for their own power generation, grid connections and infrastructure. Slower permitting could reduce incremental MW, but the electrical content per MW built could rise.

UBS Knowledge Network's 'Bring Your Own Power' basket (UBXXBYOP, 17 names, excludes utilities) targets behind-the-meter generation and enabling electrical infrastructure. UBS pitches it as a way to buy the dip in AI while positioned for the post-midterm regulatory regime.

trade_ideas.description: Buy UBS Knowledge Network 'Bring Your Own Power' basket (UBXXBYOP, 17 names) to buy the AI dip
trade_ideas.rationale: Exposure to behind-the-meter generation and electrical infrastructure while still long AI capex, positioned for the post-midterm regulatory regime.

risk_factors: Sovereign debt repricing triggered by a political event, with France the leading candidate.
Hotter inflation leading to more Fed tightening, including a possible 50bp December hike.
Weak European consumer and limited pricing power amid cost inflation.
Australian earnings downgrades and a hawkish RBA with rates at 15-year highs.
Continued AI-trade volatility and sharp de-grossing days.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility of gross hedge fund flows is higher than at any point in UBS Knowledge Network history. It began rising in late 2024 and has stayed elevated this year despite index vol trending lower.
Gross exposure remains elevated in the US and Europe. De-grossing days are followed by re-grossing.
Short exposure has risen rapidly and is at highs across the US and Europe, raising the chance of an unloved rally into year end.
Nets are tighter through increased hedging after faster trading and bruised PnLs.
Hedge-fund USD positioning remains relatively light despite BBDXY at one-year highs.
95th-percentile daily rise in US 2-year yields is about 13bp versus 5.8bp in the 2010s.
geopolitical: French fiscal and political risk: a narrow political path to reassuring bond markets, with France seen as the next test for sovereign debt.
US midterm elections shifting policy toward hyperscalers supplying their own power.
Reference to the market reaction after Liberation Day in April 2025 and the Liz Truss episode as examples of political events triggering sovereign debt repricing.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets may keep tolerating deteriorating fundamentals as long as politicians tinker at the edges and signal fiscal restraint.
tension_points.bear_case: Sovereign yields keep grinding higher and gold remains the hedge against an eventual series of debt crises. A political event can force a sudden repricing, with France the likely next test.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A political decision that forces the bond market to confront France's fiscal arithmetic.

tension_points.bull_case: Short exposure is at highs across the US and Europe, so good or no news could trigger an unloved rally into year end.
tension_points.bear_case: Hedge fund activity is likely to be muted and gross exposure volatility is at record highs, with sharp de-grossing days recurring.

tension_points.bull_case: Even if permitting slows incremental MW, the electrical content per MW built could rise, supporting AI power spend.
tension_points.bear_case: More scrutiny of data centres and policy pressure on hyperscalers to supply their own power could slow deployment.
